findings.risk: Shared design/MODEL_POINTS.json unprotected read-modify-write and common MODEL_POINTS.tmp can lose entries or collide across arms.
MODEL_LEASE.lock uses LOCK_NB across whole model worker. Overlapping C0/C1 canary inference rejects one worker rather than waiting.

findings.finding: Global completed update append uses LOCK_EX and fsync with cap validation under lock.

findings.risk: Preupdate read is unlocked; concurrent write/read could expose partial lines or a stale precap snapshot. Distinct arm and per-arm update caps reduce aggregate overshoot risk but do not protect this read.

findings.finding: Exact base root/learning/<arm>; passing proof and path containment required; only that arm continuous8/split4/split8 deleted after proof. Different arms isolated.

findings.risk: Outer C0 driver owns accepted PBS process and allocation lifecycle. At ARM_START_STOP, it can close allocation and exit while separately launched C1 remains active; scheduler cleanup can terminate C1.
No shared arm ownership lock protects an additional caller against main driver invoking same C1 before ARM_START_STOP. Native fresh-process receipts detect duplicates only after they exist.

owner_decision: No concurrent C1 process or live code change; prioritize C0 endpoint and original qualification/confirmation.
